failures.criterion: skills/dispatch/SKILL.md, "Close what you opened": the trim that brought the three Dispatch skills under the word guard dropped a rule the old text gave an agent. An ask made moot by anything other than another answer or a later write now carries no instruction to resolve it.
failures.evidence:
Old, two bullets: "An ask you opened is yours until answered or resolved. If it is answered another way or made moot, `dispatch resolve-ask` it that turn." and "Resolve each open ask a later write names that is no longer needed; retract one a new ask replaces." New: "An ask you opened is yours until answered or resolved. `dispatch resolve-ask` it that turn when another answer or a later write makes it needless." and "Retract an ask a new one replaces."

Rule by rule: ownership until answered or resolved is kept; "answered another way" is kept as "another answer ... makes it needless"; "a later write names that is no longer needed" is kept as "a later write makes it needless"; the retraction is kept. What has no counterpart is "or made moot". The old trigger named no cause; the new one enumerates two. An ask made moot by neither - the work is dropped, a person settles it over Envoy, the blocker disappears, the issue is parked - is exactly the stale ask this section exists to close, and it is now uninstructed. These skills are loaded by every session with Dispatch, so the loss reaches every agent.

Remedy and its cost: restoring "or made moot" is 3 words against 2 words of headroom (the three skills are 1,998 of a guard that demands fewer than 2,000, measured with wc -w and with the guard's own test). So it needs at least 2 words cut elsewhere in skills/dispatch, skills/dispatch-first or skills/dispatch-writing-specs, which is the same trade the round already made once.

pushWithoutTheTrailer: This tester's handoff push touches only .legion/INFRA-745/, so skill://legion-worker would have it end with `skip-checks: true`. It deliberately does not, and the reason given at the time - that a trailered head had suppressed the run for the whole previous push - did not survive its own test: the untrailered push started no run either. So the deviation bought nothing. It cost nothing either, since no run started and the daemon classifies a push by the paths its commits touch rather than by the trailer, so this push is still handoff-only to the daemon. Recorded here rather than quietly dropped, because the next role should take the ordinary rule and write the trailer on a handoff-only push.
